fixture.change_summary: Adds a retry wrapper around the billing client and a one-off notice to affected customers.

findings.description: An unused `import { backoff } from './util'` was left in src/billing/retry.js. It is dead code with no runtime effect; a git revert removes it entirely and nothing of it remains.

test/billing-retry.test.js asserts 3 attempts but the wrapper only retries twice, so the test fails. The defect is entirely in the diff under review; a git revert of the merge commit restores the prior passing state and leaves nothing behind.

On deploy, scripts/notify.js sends a one-off email to every affected customer's real address announcing the billing change. The emails are dispatched to external recipients during the rollout; a git revert removes the script but cannot un-send the messages already delivered — the external effect persists after revert.

question: For each finding, decide fail or needs-human by the revert test.
_comment: Exercises the all-fail side (two revert-reversible defects) alongside an irreversible external effect (sent emails -> needs-human, persists after revert).
